assessment_summary: The proof contains a structural algebraic flaw in part (iii) when calculating the flow value. It assumes that the net flow out of the source `s` can be computed simply by summing the flow on all outgoing edges from `s`, effectively ignoring any flow on incoming edges to `s`. While it is a common simplification to assume sources have no incoming edges, general flow networks do not forbid them. When evaluating the proof on a valid network containing an incoming edge to `s`, the specific algebraic claims on lines 0118-0130 evaluate to demonstrably false statements (e.g., 0 = 2), breaking the proof's justification for why the constructed flow `h` has value `|g| - |f|`.
counterexample:
Graph G = (V, E)
Vertices: V = {s, a, b, t}
Edges: E = {(s, a), (a, b), (b, s), (b, t)}
Capacities: c(e) = 10 for all e in E.
(This is a standard valid flow network with no anti-parallel edges.)

Flow f:
f(s, a) = 2, f(a, b) = 2, f(b, s) = 2, f(b, t) = 0
Conservation holds at `a` (2 in, 2 out) and `b` (2 in, 2 out).
Net flow from s: |f| = f(s, a) - f(b, s) = 2 - 2 = 0.

Flow g:
g(s, a) = 5, g(a, b) = 5, g(b, s) = 3, g(b, t) = 2
Conservation holds at `a` (5 in, 5 out) and `b` (5 in, 5 out).
Net flow from s: |g| = g(s, a) - g(b, s) = 5 - 3 = 2.
We have |g| > |f| since 2 > 0.

The proof claims on lines 0118-0121:
`|f| = \sum_{y: (s->y)\in E} f(s, y)`
Substituting our values:
Left side is |f| = 0.
Right side is f(s, a) = 2.
0 = 2 is FALSE.

The proof claims on lines 0127-0130:
`|g| - |f| = \sum_{y: (s->y)\in E} [ g(s, y) - f(s, y) ]`
Substituting our values:
Left side: |g| - |f| = 2 - 0 = 2.
Right side: g(s, a) - f(s, a) = 5 - 2 = 3.
2 = 3 is FALSE.
